findings.title: Test only covers a round number
findings.explanation: 3000 cents split into thirds gives exactly 2000, so this test never exercises the Math.round path in proratedAmount. Consider an amount that doesn't divide evenly, for example 1000 cents after ten days of a thirty-day period. That would pin down the rounding behavior. The PR title mentions a partial month, so this is where rounding matters most.

findings.title: Repeated fixture setup
findings.explanation: The same start and end dates are redeclared in every test. Hoisting them to shared constants in the describe block, or using it.each for the boundary cases, would reduce duplication. This is optional.

findings.title: Degenerate period not covered
findings.explanation: If periodStart equals periodEnd, total is 0 and proratedAmount divides by zero, which returns NaN. This is an edge case the PR doesn't cover. Consider either a test and a guard in the implementation, or confirm that it can't happen.
